fact: Contemporary accounts describe the Delta Air Lines Flight 841 hijacking as a flight from Detroit to Algeria that was diverted under gunpoint and flown on to other stops before reaching Algeria, with passengers and crew held during the ordeal and later released there.
During the hijacking of Delta Air Lines Flight 841, Wright and his accomplices demanded a $1 million ransom.

Contemporary reporting said Delta Flight 841 was commandeered around 12:45 p.m. over Orlando after departing Detroit for Miami, and the hijackers collected a $1 million ransom before flying on to Algeria.

The confirmed ransom paid was $1 million, and the FBI later said the money and plane were returned to the United States by Algeria, with no recovery of the money from the hijackers themselves documented in the source set here.

On July 31, 1972, the hijackers seized Delta Air Lines Flight 841, concealed a firearm in a hollowed-out Bible, demanded $1 million, and ordered the aircraft diverted to Algeria, where the incident ended after the ransom and passengers were released.

The hijackers demanded $1 million in ransom, and the amount was handed over during the ordeal before the passengers were released in Algeria, though the available reports do not specify later recovery of the money.

The FBI says George Edward Wright is wanted for unlawful flight to avoid confinement, air piracy, and aiding and abetting, reflecting the federal response to his 1970 escape and 1972 hijacking.

George Edward Wright escaped from a New Jersey prison in August 1970, joined the Black Liberation Army, hijacked Delta Air Lines Flight 841 on July 31, 1972, and was arrested in Portugal on September 26, 2011 after more than 40 years as a fugitive.
The FBI lists George Edward Wright’s offenses as unlawful flight to avoid confinement, escape (murder), air piracy, and aiding and abetting.
A fingerprint found on Wright’s Portuguese ID card matched records in a national Portuguese database, which led U.S. authorities and Portuguese police to locate and arrest him in September 2011.
